original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Test the Cartesian source-destination grid identity A_(i,1)=X_i, B_(1,j)=Y_j, which produces r^2 block products from one generic width-r matrix-product child. Bound its recursive-work saving for every 2<=r<=51 and 0<=a<=1/99, granting all data movement and interface expenses for free.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card starts from one-dimensional block frame climbs. This experiment changes the output geometry to a full Cartesian grid and derives a separate quadratic matrix-product cost model, so the incumbent linear paid-mass ceiling is not applied outside its hypotheses.
bottleneck_link: A larger-rank child can reduce recursive work only if its larger block output offsets the full r^(2-a) matrix-product charge. The exact best-case grid ratio is at least 19/20 throughout the target exponent range under the rank-51 guard, below the task's 5% screening threshold even before interface costs.
stop_rule: Bound every width r=2..51 at 0<=a<=1/99. Stop before selected-word synthesis if the free-interface generic block's exact best-case saving is below 5%; restart only for a changed child contract or cost law.
evidence: verify.py passes 15 exact formal-polynomial identity fixtures, two block-placement mutation controls, exact integer-power tests for the 5% threshold, and an integer 99th-root decimal bracket. Maximum saving is <5%; first width reaching 5% is 161.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in selecting the mechanism, deriving the cost bound, implementing exact controls, and writing the package.

open_questions.question: Can a changed child contract use a cheaper bilinear algorithm for a Cartesian grid while preserving the selected provider's arbitrary dirty state and frame endpoints?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A different admitted interface is the only route from this grid geometry to a recursive-work improvement beyond the generic width-r cost bound.
open_questions.first_step: Check an exact small-width tensor decomposition and compute its full source, copy, frame, output, and restoration invoice.
